scope: Proposition 2.2 (Finite affine comparisons) of the manuscript “The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model” (preprints/The-critical-logarithmic-correction-for-the-planar-XY-model-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5c357d1c416119fa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 5-6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On every fixed primary graph, the Bessel height law has the following properties. (i) A shifted-to-centered partition ratio is at most one and decreases when the same nonnegative quadratic precision is added to the affine and centered coordinates. Affine data may include an integral connection, observation centers, and compatible nonzero equality values. The monotonicity remains valid with a fixed real linear statistic in the numerator exponent, although the tilted ratio need not be at most one. 5 (ii) For zero affine data, centered covariances and centered real moment generating functions decrease under added centered precision. Centered characteristic coefficients allowed by the constant convention in both laws are nonnegative and increase under added precision. They are strictly positive for the finite-graph phases used below, whose coefficient total on every unconfined component is an integer. (iii) If X = P e qe∇eh in a centered law, then Var X ≤ Cb X e q2 e , E|X|k ≤ Ck,b X e q2 e !k/2 . More generally, after releasing endpoint, curl, and period constraints while re- taining independent primary increments, a tilt with maxe |qe| ≤ K costs at most exp(Cb,K P e q2 e). The statements include independent Gaussian observation noises. Released constants are taken modulo translations or confined; a real statistic used in releasing a constant must annihilate it.
